title: Descent of opens along an fpqc covering
statement: Let $\{g_i:T_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ be an fpqc covering [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering], and let $V\to S$ be etale. If opens $W_i\subset T_i\times_S V$ have equal pullbacks to $T_i\times_S T_j\times_S V$ for all $i,j$, then there is a unique open $W\subset V$ whose pullback to every $T_i\times_S V$ is $W_i$.

proof.text: By stability of fpqc coverings under base change [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change], the family of second projections $T_i\times_S V\to V$ is an fpqc covering of $V$. In Lean, Presieve.ofArrows_pullback identifies this family with the pullback presieve, and Precoverage.pullbackArrows_mem transports the covering hypothesis.

Apply the compatible-open descent statement [lem-weil-pbc-open-subscheme-fpqc-descent] to this base-changed covering and the opens $W_i\subset T_i\times_S V$. The Lean hypothesis already uses the double pullbacks of the second projections, so it is exactly the compatibility hypothesis of openSubscheme_existsUnique_of_fpqc. These pullbacks [def-pc-fibre-product] identify canonically with the triple products in the node statement. The descent theorem supplies existence and uniqueness together.
